# 大乘起信論略述

**ID:** T2813
**Volume:** T85
**Category:** 論集部類,敦煌寫本部類
**Original Category:** 古逸部
**Byline:** 唐 曇曠撰
**Dynasty:** 唐
**Date:** 618–907
**Juans:** 2
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T2813

## Contributors
- 曇曠 (A001803)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A two-*juǎn* late-Tang Yogācāra commentary on the *Awakening of Faith* by [曇曠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E6%9B%A0) Tánkuàng (fl. c. 770–790), a senior Yogācāra scholar of the Cháng'ān Xīmíngsì 西明寺 who in 774 produced a *Bǎifǎ míngmén kāizōng yìjué* and was active in the Héxī corridor (modern Wǔwēi 武威) propagating the Faxiang school. Recovered through the Dūnhuáng cache and printed in Taishō Vol. 85 (the so-called 古逸部 / 疑似部 — Taishō's archive of "antique-recovered" and "doubtful" texts).

**Abstract**

The text opens with a preface by 沙門澄漪 Chéng-yī ("the monk of Limpid Ripples") commending Tán-kuàng's commentary: "Perfect awakening was hidden in obscurity, and heterodox learnings rose like peaks. Without a proper exposition, the Right Dharma would have been distorted. Therefore the great being Aśvaghoṣa expounded *paramārtha-satya*, drawing together the various śāstras and binding the multiple sūtras, breaking the two extremes and harmonizing the Middle Way, composing this treatise to encourage future ages." The preface continues: "There is a monk, Tán-kuàng of Jiàn-kāng [region], young and fond of learning, mature and accomplished in virtue, profound in his comprehension of the meaning…"

Tán-kuàng's commentary takes up the *Awakening of Faith* from a Yogācāra-school standpoint: he has a strong interest in the relation between the *ālayavijñāna* / *Tathāgatagarbha* identification, in line with his Xī-míng-sì training under the line of [圓測](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%B8%AC) Yuán-cè. The text was unknown in mainstream East Asian Buddhism for centuries, surviving only in the Dūnhuáng cache; it has therefore not entered the canonical commentarial dialogue developed by [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) and [子璿](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%90%E7%92%BF). Composition is bracketed by Tán-kuàng's documented activity period 770–800.

The Taishō establishes the text from the Dūnhuáng manuscript witnesses, base 高麗 absent, collated against the Dūnhuáng 甲 manuscript variants.
